Decision guide

An AI vendor security questionnaire for procurement

Your legal team uploads a synthetic contract into a trial workspace. An employee in another department searches for its filename. This simple exercise gives procurement a precise opening question: which permissions did the system check before returning the result?

Follow one test document

  1. IngestIdentify each copy
  2. ProcessTrace who can read it
  3. DeleteVerify what remains

On this page

Trace one request across the serviceSeparate what you tested from what the vendor promisedTest a change, then record the responseDecision tableWorked buyer scenarioMake the decision

Trace one request across the service

Ask the vendor to draw the request path from upload to response. Label each copy of the material, including extracted text, embeddings, support logs and backups. Beside each copy, record the owner, location, access rules and retention interval. If the model provider changes between product tiers, ask the vendor to identify the tier described by its answer.

Separate what you tested from what the vendor promised

At the review meeting, give each answer one evidence type. A screen recording can show that a user lost access after a role change. A contract clause can define when backup copies expire. The recording alone does not prove when a backup was erased. Give unresolved items an owner who can obtain the missing evidence.

Test a change, then record the response

Move the synthetic file to a restricted group, revoke the uploader and repeat the search as a second user. Check generated summaries and shared links as well as the original file. Ask support to locate the associated audit event by request ID. Record timestamps and the product version so that another reviewer can repeat the test.

Decision table
Question to sendEvidence to attach
Who can retrieve a file after group access is removed?Two test identities and the observed before/after result.
Which copies survive deletion?Retention schedule per system, exception owner and contract reference.
Who can view customer prompts in support?Support-access approval flow and a redacted example event.
What changes when a subprocessor changes?Notification mechanism, responsible contact and review window.

Illustrative buyer scenario

What survives a deletion request?

A procurement team uploads a dummy contract containing a unique fictional reference. The vendor deletes the original during a review meeting. The team still needs a list of indexes, logs, backups and support tools that might retain a copy before its data owner signs the contract.

Ask the vendor to trace the test reference through each documented component. Record whether deletion is immediate, scheduled, or governed by backup expiry. Give every outstanding question an owner and a deadline.

What to keep

A dated data-flow diagram, role-specific retrieval results and written retention terms for each component that can hold a copy.

When to pause

Keep the application outside the sensitive workflow if nobody can identify the responsible party for a downstream copy.

Make the decision

The decision record should name the permitted data classes and the unresolved conditions. A team can approve a synthetic-data pilot while it waits for evidence about production customer records. Review those conditions again before anyone uploads live documents.
